newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit consolidates, baht firm.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Ringgit consolidates, baht firm.

text.p: * Malaysian ringgit sees balanced buying and selling demand as market moves into consolidation phase.
* Thai baht finds healthy domestic support ahead of holiday as central bank sets mid-rate at new low of 26.07.
* Singapore dollar stablises after U.S. hedge fund selling in early market.
* Indonesian rupiah stable, focus remains on liquidity and demand ahead of new bank reserve requirements.
The Malaysian ringgit traded in a stable range on Friday, balanced by demand from Kuala Lumpur corporate buyers and foreign funds, dealers said.
"There's a continuation of some dollar buying from U.S. funds and a cap on dollar rally because of expected bank intervention," one dealer with a Japanese bank said.
U.S. demand was thought related to a one-year outright deal, keeping the dollar/ringgit in a 2.5000/2.5080 range.
Bank Negara Malaysia was seen likely to step in above 2.5100 for ringgit, capping the rate, as it was believed to have done on Wednesday when the ringgit fell to 2.5120.
The Thai baht was stable and supported by retail demand ahead of a four-day Songkran holiday next week.
Speculation U.S. funds were showing interest in the baht after a spell of nervousness also aided sentiment.
"We're hearing that hedge funds are showing interest about going into the basket again," a Singapore bank dealer said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at another new low of 26.07 against moves in dollar/yen.
The baht was quoted at 26.073/26.078 to the dollar at 0410 GMT against 26.065/26.085 late Thursday.
Indonesia's rupiah was steady in thin activity with sentiment underpinned by new bank reserve requirements for April 16.
Some dealers said they did not expect much tightening as many banks were well prepared, but others said liquidity was still in question and swap rates could see further declines.
Dollar/rupiah was at 2,406.00/2,406.70, up from the morning's 2,406.80/2,406.50.
"The rupiah should range between 2,404 and 2,408 in the near-term, with a firming bias," a Singapore-based dealer said.
He said a drain in rupiah and dollars could ensue next week as banks focused on the new reserve rules and monthly tax payments.
Bank Indonesia raised the intervention band by one point to 2,399/2,591 and the conversion band to 2,399/2,447 on Thursday.
In Singapore, dollar/Sing stablised after an initial fall on the back of early selling from one U.S. major, dealers said.
But traders said the range remained narrow, caught between U.S. dollar buying interest below 1.4350 and local corporate selling interest around 1.4450.
Overall, the lack of any central bank intervention was seen leading the Singapore dollar back down to re-test recent lows of 1.4520 in the face of the U.S. unit's continued bull run.
-- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-206 2323), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), James Mclean in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Jacqueline Wong in Singapore (65-8703090)
